comment: How forge builds this repository (nzions/nanokvm, the fork of sipeed/NanoKVM). forge reads this out of
the tree it just cloned and runs the named profile's `run` once. There is no trunk block yet: a push
does nothing by itself, a build is requested by hand (forge_build repo=nanokvm).
check  a cheap gate: gofmt over server/ (vendor/ excluded) and go vet of the update-signature
verifier, the one package whose breakage bricks updates on devices.
test   go test of every server/ package that carries a _test.go (vendor/ excluded), on the host arch:
-tags nokvm swaps common/kvm_vision.go (cgo, links the riscv64-only dl_lib/libkvm.so) for its stub.
build  the riscv64 release, the same steps `make release` runs in docker, without docker. Runs in the
`c` image (forge-c >= 1.26 carries the NanoKVM toolchains at /opt, opt-in: Sophgo host-tools,
Go 1.26.0, Node + pnpm). scripts/forge-build.sh does the work and writes
/artifacts is the repo's artifacts share (/data/nfs/artifacts/nanokvm on beefy). A published
version is never overwritten with different bytes. The result is UNSIGNED: sign the printed
The version comes from CHANGELOG.md (or an exact numeric git tag, or $NANOKVM_VERSION).
`bash`, not `sh`: the script and build-in-container.sh use bash.
The build uses no MaixCDK and downloads nothing (forge-build.sh fails closed if it does);
8 CPUs / 8g is a first guess, forge_stats will say what it used.

check.run: bad=$(find server -name '*.go' -not -path 'server/vendor/*' -print0 | xargs -0 gofmt -l) && { [ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "gofmt needed:"; echo "$bad"; exit 1; }; } && cd server && go vet ./service/updatesign/

test.run: cd server && go test -count=1 -tags nokvm $(find . -name '*_test.go' -not -path './vendor/*' -exec dirname {} \; | sort -u)
